title: Two heaps & K-way merge
learn: max-heap + min-heap for running median; merging k sorted lists with a heap
hook: Find Median from Data Stream and Merge k Sorted Lists are two famous hards that become manageable once you see the heap trick behind each: split the data into two halves, or keep one candidate per source.

explain.prompt: Explain how two heaps give you the running median of a stream, and how a heap merges k sorted lists.
keyPoints: median: max-heap for the lower half, min-heap for the upper half; every lower value ≤ every upper value
keep sizes equal (or the lower heap one larger); median = lower top, or the average of both tops
each insert is O(log n), the median is O(1)
k-way merge: a min-heap holds the current head of each list; pop the smallest, push that list's next element
merge costs O(N log k) for N total elements
